page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Page number and running head at the top left. Faint marks in the lower left margin (a "(1)" and a small "M") and a smudge at the foot left, which I read as scan or edge marks, not printed text.

main_text.p: reditum concederent, rursum commoti Græci, quibus id contra opinionem accidebat, & tyrannicum dominatum contra leges sapere videbatur, in arma versi sunt. Unde bellum Lamiacum~ quod dictum, fuit ortum, gestum anno proximo à morte Alexandri contra eundem Antipatrum, principibus civitate Atticâ & Ætolis. Quod desiit tandem in oppressionem libertatis Atticæ, & dominatum Antipatri: de quo dictum in rebus Athenien-sium~. Interea flaccescente virtutis vigore apud Spartanos, quod reliquum ejus erat, ab Areo rege, Pyrrhi Epirotæ, inclyti bellatoris coætaneo, & ejusce filio Acrotato, extinctum periit. Hi enim phiditiorum morem, ut nos docet Athenæus, solverunt, & à victu parco, qui in phiditiis usurpabatur, in delitias, & effusum epularum luxum~, exemplo & autoritate præeuntes, civium cœnas traduxerunt. Inde in omnem molliciem, & quæ eam comitantur vitia, civitas prolapsa pristinæ disciplinæ & severi moris nihil fere retinuit. Præsertim cum Leonidas, qui post Acrotatum pro filio ejus Areo juniore impubere regnum administravit, & post mortem ejus rex factus fuit, prædecef-forum

page.notes: The text runs on from the previous page and ends mid-word at the foot: "prædecef-" with "forum" on the last line, so the word is "prædecessorum". The marks "~" after Lamiacum, Athenien-sium and luxum are printed signs, copied as they appear. "præeuntes" and "effusum" are read from the scan and may carry small doubts. The faint "(1)" and "M" in the lower left margin are not clearly legible and are not transcribed as text.
